HSTU provides distinct intervention points: relative position/time bias, content-dependent QK scores, value aggregation, and multiplicative gating. Its original formulation uses SiLU attention rather than softmax; masking must therefore follow the actual attention implementation. The 2025 study *Scaling New Frontiers* ablates relative bias, SiLU, and feature interaction, reporting particularly limited depth gains without relative bias and stronger results with temporal information than position alone. These findings motivate separate position-bias and time-bias probes, rather than treating all recency effects as content dependence. [Original HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3), [component study](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=e6pqwHR1Yh).

Suggested diagnostic design—not an established HSTU-specific protocol in these sources: freeze each category’s single model and candidate set; compare recent versus older context interventions matched for token count. Preserve sequence slots, timestamps, validity masks, and the original final nonpadding readout item/index. Pair content replacement with attention-edge blocking: replacement changes content-dependent representations while retaining positional geometry; edge blocking removes access to selected context. Separately zero position/time bias while retaining content. Report paired target-rank changes, score-margin changes, and HR@10 differences with uncertainty. Effects are model sensitivity, not causal evidence about users. Content sensitivity motivates context-dropout experiments; bias sensitivity motivates bias regularization; divergent results motivate checking masking and readout correctness. The 2026 position-bias study supports controlled positional perturbations, but does not establish this exact HSTU protocol or guarantee gains on these Amazon categories. [Position-bias study](https://repository.eduhk.hk/en/publications/diagnosing-and-mitigating-mid-sequence-degradation-in-recommender/).
